correctness.rationale: An explicit proof derives the complete 21-state Fano flag classification via degree and point–line incidence counts, rules out precisely the four other same-endpoint flags, constructs 16 ordered guard shifts in a normalized case, transports all moves by flag-transitive automorphisms, and exhibits a direct response to any possible attack from any minimum position. This establishes 21 states, 168 shifts, diameter two, and eternal four-guard defense. Independently constructed exhaustive Python verifiers check all 21 configurations, all 210 unordered pairs and all attacks using different incidence and matching algorithms. No unproved infinite generalization is claimed.

evidence: Goddard et al. (2005), https://www.researchgate.net/publication/249799004_Eternal_Security_in_Graphs, Theorem 10, asserted general equality for Cayley graphs but the argument has a documented error.

Braga et al. (2016), https://combinatorialpress.com/jcmcc-articles/volume-096/a-note-on-the-paper-eternal-security-in-graphs-by-goddard-hedetniemi-and-hedetniemi-2005/, exhibit a different graph and refute the general statement.
Carr et al. (2026), arXiv:2607.04024, Proposition 2.1/Corollary 2.2 require efficient dominating sets for their uniform equality argument.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Even if a valid general equality theorem implied the guard number, it would not determine all pairwise legal optimum-to-optimum shifts. Efficient domination requires a partition into closed neighborhoods of size four, impossible at order 14; the corrected 2016 counterexample has 18 vertices and degree six. No stronger general reconfiguration theorem was identified.

originality.rationale: The exact guard shift graph is the complement of the Heawood line graph, a statement about all 210 pairs of optimal guard configurations. A known 21-state classification under vertex-addition/deletion moves cannot determine these simultaneous guard shifts. The original 2005 generic Cayley theorem is false; the 2016 correction treats an 18-vertex 6-regular counterexample; the 2026 efficient-dominating-set theorem is inapplicable since 4 does not divide 14. Checked published mathematical research records under Heawood/Fano flag aliases yielded no covering statement. Bounded residual uncertainty about inaccessible pages and unindexed results is disclosed; priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Publisher PDF pages 8–10 of Braga et al. (2016) were unavailable during bounded retries, although the accessible main counterexample is on a distinct graph.
Unindexed or unpublished finite-state computations could contain an equivalent identification; negative bibliographic searches do not certify priority.
The enumerated 21 minimum dominating sets and the pure numerical equality are not independently claimed original.

value.rationale: The structural isomorphism to the complement of the line graph of the Heawood graph identifies the full communication structure of an optimal security game on a canonical 14-vertex symmetric incidence graph; it yields a geometric exact transition test, uniform 16-way mobility and a universal winning optimal response. These features are not merely the routine known domination number, state count, or a weak scalar refinement. The problem is defined by the natural all-guards-move rule and the classical Fano geometry, with future uses for testing guard-game strategies and constrained matching reconfiguration.
